summary: This is NOT a Playwright-specific healer — it is the Healenium backend (hlm-backend), a Spring Boot Java REST API from EPAM that stores and retrieves selector healing data via PostgreSQL. The actual healing algorithm lives in a separate dependency (com.epam.healenium:tree-comparing) that compares DOM page trees to find alternative broken-locator candidates. The backend exposes REST endpoints (POST /healenium to save known selectors, POST /healenium/healing to persist healing attempts, GET /healenium/healing to retrieve scored alternative locators) and serves a Thymeleaf admin UI for managing selectors. Core entities: Selector (locator + node path, identified by a compound key of locator/URL/command), Healing (a healing attempt tied to pageContent), and HealingResult (scored alternative locator candidates). There is zero Playwright-specific code, zero Playwright imports, and the selenium-java dependency reveals its Selenium origins. Playwright would interact with this only via HTTP, which requires the full Healenium stack (client plugin + this backend + Postgres + optional S3 metrics sink).

maturityAssessment.contradictionFlags: CRITICAL: The repo folder is named 'playwright-healer' but the source code, README, dependencies, and architecture are all for 'healenium-backend' (hlm-backend) — a Selenium-era self-healing backend with ZERO Playwright bindings. The actual healing engine (tree-comparing) lives in a SEPARATE dependency (com.epam.healenium:tree-comparing:0.4.14), not in this repository. This repo is just a REST CRUD wrapper around PostgreSQL tables. What you get is a persistent storage layer for DOM locators — not a Playwright-healing library.

findings.description: 1. Selector registration and inventory (POST /healenium): saves known selectors with their locator type/value, node path, URL, and Selenium command. 2. Selector lookup with node paths (GET /healenium): returns the last-known DOM node paths for a selector — used by the client to re-locate elements when the original locator breaks. 3. Healing persistence (POST /healenium/healing): stores healing attempts with scored alternative locators, original page content, and session tracking. 4. Scored result retrieval (GET /healenium/healing/results): returns the best alternative locators ranked by score (from the tree-comparing algorithm). 5. Healing success/failure bucketing (POST /healenium/healing/success): clients call back to report whether a healed locator actually worked, enabling healing effectiveness tracking. 6. S3 metrics push: optionally pushes healing success/failure metrics to an S3 bucket for analytics. 7. Selector migration (GET /healenium/migrate): re-computes selector IDs when configuration changes (e.g. toggling URL inclusion in keys). 8. Thymeleaf admin UI (GET /healenium/selectors): a web interface to toggle healing on/off per selector. 9. Config management (GET /healenium/elements): returns configuration of which selectors have healing enabled/disabled.
findings.evidence: 1. Selector registration and inventory (POST /healenium): saves known selectors with their locator type/value, node path, URL, and Selenium command. 2. Selector lookup with node paths (GET /healenium)

apiSurface: REST API at port 7878: GET /healenium - get reference elements (node paths) for a locator. POST /healenium - save a known working locator. GET /healenium/healing - retrieve healing results for a selector. POST /healenium/healing - persist healing attempts with candidate locators. GET /healenium/healing/results - get scored healing results. POST /healenium/healing/success - report whether a healing worked. GET /healenium/elements - get all selectors and their healing config. POST /healenium/selector/status - toggle healing on/off. GET /healenium/selectors — Thymeleaf admin UI page. POST /healenium/session - restore session for proxy mode. GET /healenium/migrate - migrate selectors. Request headers must include SESSION_KEY_V1 or SESSION_KEY_V2 for per-healing grouping. The DTO models (RequestDto, SelectorRequestDto, HealingRequestDto with Locator objects {value, type}) define the exact JSON schema expected by REST endpoints.
integrationPoints: For a Veridian pipeline with Playwright + a job queue: 1) This backend could store historic locator to node_path mappings for laptop product pages, so when a locator becomes stale the NodePath data enables smart DNS re-locating. 2) The tree-comparing engine (external dependency) could re-rank candidate locators against a known stable DOM snapshot, but this is a black-box — Veridian would need to wrap or reimplement it. 3) Integration requires a healenium-client compatible plugin to send HTTP calls — there is none for Playwright; a custom client would be needed. 4) The S3 metrics integration (AmazonRestService) demonstrates a pattern for shipping healing stats to cloud storage, which mirrors Veridian's data needs. 5) Session-key-based result grouping aligns with per-laptop-scan pipeline runs. 6) The NodePathWrapper could store the DOM preamble position of product specs, mapping directly to Veridian's price/spec extraction from product listing pages.
strengthsForVeridian: Proven selector-healing persistence model: Selector, Healing, HealingResult with locator scoring mirrors Veridian's need to track which extraction patterns work vs. fail over time. EPAM enterprise backing means the schema design and REST API have been production-tested. The node-path approach (storing DOM paths alongside locators) is directly relevant to Veridian's architecture problem of reliable DOM data extraction when laptop product pages change structure. The success/failure webhook pattern creates a closed-loop feedback system that Veridian could repurpose into an ETL pattern-scoring loop. Does not lock Veridian into a specific selector strategy — only stores whatever locators Veridian tracks.
weaknessesForVeridian: The name 'playwright-healer' is a complete misnomer — there are zero Playwright imports, zero Playwright clients, and zero Playwright documentation. The selenium-java dependency and findElement/findElements gating reveal it was designed for Selenium, not Playwright. The actual healing algorithm (tree-comparing) is in a separate closed-source-like library at version 0.4.14 — this repo stores results, it does not heal anything. It requires the entire Healenium stack (client plugin + this Spring Boot backend + PostgreSQL + optional S3) — can't be used standalone. The Spring Boot/JPA/Thymeleaf stack is heavy overkill for what amounts to a CRUD wrapper. The headers-based session key convention adds fragility. Port 7878 hardcoded. No typed client SDK or OpenAPI spec — callers must reverse-engineer the DTO models from Java source. Heavily dependent on PostgreSQL JSONB type (not portable to SQLite or lighter databases).
